sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Shiv Prakash
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Shiv Ji Tiwari
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Case called out in revised list.
None present on behalf of the informant.
However, learned AGA for the State is present.
2. Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Upendra Kumar Singh, Advocate holding brief of Sri Shiv Prakash Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Pradeep Kumar, learned AGA for the State.
4. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 464 of 2018, under Sections 363, 366, 376, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Bilari, District Moradabad during pendency of the trial.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits, this is third bail application filed on behalf of the applicant.

The first bail application of the applicant was dismissed by this Court on merit vide order dated 17.07.2019 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 14133 of 2019 and his second bail Kunwarpal vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19153532/
1 application was also dismissed by this Court vide order dated 29.04.2022 passed in Criminal Misc.
Bail Application No. 13724 of 2020 and applicant in the present matter is in jail since 25.11.2018 i.e.
for last more than five years and till date trial of the case could not be concluded.

sentences.text: However, in the month of April, 2023 statement of PW-6 was recorded by the trial court but after that none of the prosecution witness could be appeared before the trial court, therefore, it appears that trial of the case is moving with languid pace and there is no hope of its early disposal.

6. He further submits that as applicant is in jail, therefore, he cannot be attributed the role of delay in trial, therefore, considering the delay in trial and long incarceration of the applicant and the fact that applicant is not having any criminal history, he may be released on bail.

7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submits that this is third bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and his first two bail applications have already been dismissed by this Court on merit but could not dispute the fact that applicant is in jail for last more than five years and till date trial of the case could not be concluded.
8.
He further could not dispute the fact that as victim of the case has already been examined by the trial court, therefore, there is no chance of tampering with the prosecution evidence.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. However, this is third bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and earlier two bail applications of the applicant have already been dismissed by this Court on merit but from the record, it reflects that applicant is in jail since 25.11.2018 i.e. for last more than five years and trial of the case could not be concluded till date.
11.
Learned counsel for the applicant during the course of argument produced the certified copy of the order-sheet of the case from 06.04.2023 to 30.10.2023, which is taken on record and marked as 'A'.

From its perusal, it reflects that PW-6 was examined on 06.04.2023 and after that dates are being fixed for prosecution evidence but none of the prosecution witness appeared before the trial court, therefore, I find force in the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that trial of the case is moving with languid pace and there is no hope of its early disposal.

12. Further, applicant is not having any criminal history to his credit and in the present matter he is in jail since 25.11.2018 i.e. for last more than five years and it also reflects from the record that victim of the case has already been examined by the trial court, therefore, there is no chance of tampering with the prosecution evidence.

13. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

sentences.text:
Let the applicant - Kunwarpal be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 15.12.2023 AK Pandey  Kunwarpal vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19153532/
